nodes.description: DDRGK1 interacts with the kinase domain of the ER stress sensor IRE1-alpha (ERN1) and protects it from ubiquitin-dependent degradation in a UFMylation-dependent manner. Loss of DDRGK1, or mutation of its K268 UFMylation site, reduces IRE1-alpha UFMylation and increases ubiquitylation-mediated IRE1-alpha degradation. This branch was described in cancer cells and haematopoietic stem cells in 2017 and extended to chondrocytes and the growth plate in 2023.

nodes.description: SOX9 is normally polyubiquitinated and turned over by the proteasome. nodes.description: Deleting Ddrgk1 in the aggrecan lineage in early postnatal mice severely retards spinal growth, disrupts disc cellularity and initiates disc degeneration, with apoptosis, extracellular-matrix disruption and ER stress in both nucleus pulposus and cartilage endplate; adult deletion thins the cartilage endplate. This is mouse evidence only. It is recorded because the human disease is defined by vertebral abnormalities (platyspondyly with central vertebral hypoplasia) and no other node reaches the spine, but no patient disc or vertebral tissue has been examined.

nodes.description: Cartilage-lineage deletion that survives to show the growth plate. Mutants develop progressive severe limb shortening and joint abnormalities; the growth plate is disorganised with a shortened proliferative and enlarged hypertrophic zone, Sox9 and Col2a1 protein are reduced and Col10a1 expanded. Osteoblast-specific deletion with Osteocalcin-Cre or Leptin receptor-Cre produced no bone phenotype, locating the defect in cartilage. The authors state the models recapitulate the patients' short stature and joint abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: DDRGK1 is required for the proper development and maintenance of the growth plate cartilage.
evidence.snippet: To investigate the cartilage-specific role of DDRGK1, conditional knockout mice were generated by intercrossing Prx1-Cre transgenic mice with Ddrgkfl/fl mice to delete its expression in limb mesenchymal cells.

nodes.description: SOX9 is the master transcription factor of chondrogenesis and COL2A1 its direct target. In ddrgk1-deficient zebrafish, Ddrgk1-null mouse limb buds and Ddrgk1-knockdown ATDC5 chondrogenic cells, SOX9 protein and Col2a1 transcript fall; in Prx1-Cre conditional knockout growth plates Sox9 and Col2a1 protein are reduced while Col10a1 expands. The reduction in SOX9 is less than 50 per cent in null mice, yet the skeletal phenotype exceeds that of Sox9 haploinsufficiency, which the discovery paper reads as DDRGK1 acting on targets beyond SOX9.
